extraction.name: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating temporal understanding capabilities of multimodal large language models using 20 video understanding tasks. It is built by automatically converting public video annotations into multiple-choice QA pairs from 11 public video datasets.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were selected from 11 public video benchmarks and automatically converted into multiple-choice QA pairs using task definitions and LLMs. The paper describes a static-to-dynamic task design and an automatic annotation paradigm with ChatGPT to generate questions and answer options from existing public annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public video datasets/benchmarks including STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Static tasks were adapted into dynamic temporal tasks; questions were augmented with temporal context; answer options were constructed from ground-truth annotations or generated with ChatGPT; options were randomly sampled and shuffled, and similar-length options were enforced to reduce answer leakage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered for temporal sensitivity and difficulty: short clips were removed, extremely long videos were removed, intermediate-duration videos were selected (primarily 5s to 35s), and dataset-specific filtering criteria were applied (e.g., duration constraints, removing overly complex CLEVRER questions).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses automatic QA generation from existing annotations. ChatGPT was used to generate questions for each video based on task definitions, and answer options were created either directly from ground-truth annotations or via LLM-based generation. For some tasks, questions and answers were directly adopted from the source datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports using multiple-choice QA instead of open-ended answers for evaluation correctness and fairness, avoiding biased scoring by LLMs. It also states that answer options were shuffled and length-balanced to prevent leakage and improve robustness.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that all models and data are publicly available at the project GitHub repository and that a leaderboard is maintained on Hugging Face; no explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes videos involving persons and tasks related to actions, poses, navigation, and character order, but the paper does not state that sensitive human attributes were collected as dataset fields.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve evaluation of temporal understanding in multimodal models and to support development of more robust video MLLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing benchmarks can be biased by LLM scoring and that MVBench aims to avoid biased scoring. It also notes domain and scene diversity across first-person/third-person and indoor/outdoor videos, but no explicit dataset bias analysis is provided.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper reports that current MLLMs still struggle with position, count, character, egocentric navigation, and episodic reasoning tasks. It also notes that some tasks may require modalities beyond vision alone, such as audio or depth, and that the benchmark relies on public annotations and selected video durations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of multimodal large language models for temporal video understanding; benchmark testing and model comparison. The paper also uses the dataset for assessing baseline models such as VideoChat2.
